<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c54a23d2237dd1fce2b01f66de31d3ea33735d7c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6e32ebc5007c307ee792087fdb85fa2c8678801e` — the merge of head `16e4c087248237dfd5e77d81044b204426f51191` into base `c54a23d2237dd1fce2b01f66de31d3ea33735d7c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6e32ebc5007c307ee792087fdb85fa2c8678801e && git checkout 6e32ebc5007c307ee792087fdb85fa2c8678801e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c54a23d2237dd1fce2b01f66de31d3ea33735d7c 16e4c087248237dfd5e77d81044b204426f51191 && git checkout -B drift-repro c54a23d2237dd1fce2b01f66de31d3ea33735d7c && git merge --no-ff 16e4c087248237dfd5e77d81044b204426f51191

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c54a23d2237dd1fce2b01f66de31d3ea33735d7c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c54a23d2237dd1fce2b01f66de31d3ea33735d7c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review brief — PR #32898 @ `cf5a8840c971909a859314ddfa2f91076e63be4b` (card #32810)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.compose-stacks-flat-second-app-refused.ts packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #32810: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #32898: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `cf5a8840c971909a859314ddfa2f91076e63be4b`
  · the check-runs on `cf5a8840c971909a859314ddfa2f91076e63be4b`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.compose-stacks-flat-second-app-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6e75bbcc-4a4c-5619-8f0a-c202ed2ad733/scratchpad/pr-32898/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

Head facts, for you to verify, not to adopt:
  · Net diff: `git diff c04aa295db900486337e4a32255324ea43b03960 cf5a8840c971909a859314ddfa2f91076e63be4b` (the merge base with `main`; the head merged `main` once at that commit).
  · Check-runs on the head: 68. Two concluded `failure`: `Type Check · workspace` (job 131554007825) and `TypeScript Type Check` (job 131564106104, the type-check lane aggregator). Read both jobs' steps and logs yourself and judge what they measured.
  · The lane seat parked this PR until a release version commit lands. It will not be readied, queued or re-merged with `main` before then.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cf5a8840c971909a859314ddfa2f91076e63be4b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.compose-stacks-flat-second-app-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + none

Read for this record: card #32810 (body and its six comments), PR #32898 (body, its 11 files, the net diff from merge base `c04aa295` to the head, the 68 check-runs, and the steps and logs of both failed jobs). The implementation sits wholly inside the three `hits` files, so the second half of `Scope:` is empty. The tests, the changeset and the docs page of the diff were read as evidence and stay the lane seat's ACCEPT. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed: `packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, ADR-0019, ADR-0130 and the neighbouring semantic entry of the same rule line.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `composeStacks`, two or more inputs, a flat option (`'last'`, `'first'`, an index), selected manifest of type `app` or `module`, two or more entries in the composed `apps`: newly refused, `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION`, 422. Right wherever the result carries no `packages[]`: by ADR-0130 D4's second branch the whole artifact is then one package, and ADR-0019 D3 as amended removes a package that defines several apps. Where the result does carry `packages[]`, see ④ S1.
2. `composeStacks`, every option: a `packages[]` body of type `app` or `module` with two or more apps is newly refused. Right: each body registers under its own id (`resolveArtifactPackageEntries`).
3. `defineStack`, strict: the same body rule, newly refused. Right, and declared in the changeset and in the ADR-0087 entry. The non-strict path is unchanged.
4. `defineStack`, the stack's own package: the predicate is unchanged (the read `config.manifest?.type` that the liveness evidence quotes, more than one entry in `apps`). The finding text changes: the remedy names `composeStacks(stacks, { manifest: 'preserve' })` and the type label is derived from the type. The words "must define at most one app" remain. Right, card Work 3.
5. Envelope: no new code, class or status. A second raise site with the header `composeStacks single-app validation failed (N issues):`, one string per finding on `issues`, wrapped by `withRefusalConversions` like every other `composeStacks` refusal. The ledger's enum member, family and position are untouched (comment only). Right, and it follows the precedent `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` set: two raise sites, one code, the header naming the pass.
6. Not moved, read in the tree: a `'preserve'` composition whose inputs all carry a manifest and one app or none; a single input (returned before the options are parsed); zero inputs; a selected manifest that is absent or of another type; `strict: false` at `defineStack`. No export is added or removed, and `ComposeStacksOptionsSchema` keeps its shape (TSDoc only), so no generated reference moves.
7. ADR-0087: `registered compose-stacks-flat-second-app-refused`, a semantic entry with no D2 conversion. Right: which app stays in which package is not derivable.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/32810-compose-stacks-single-app.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` minor. That matches what the diff publishes: one package moves, and a `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` kind takes at least minor (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). The `Clause-②` declaration reads `no (narrowing)` in the PR body and in the changeset, and it is the right arm: the accept set of two exported functions narrows and nothing widens. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, the Before, Now, Unchanged and Fix paragraphs, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, whose name equals the entry's `id`. `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The two failed check-runs measured nothing about this diff.** `Type Check · workspace` (job 131554007825) timed out in step 2, `Checkout repository`, after 20 minutes inside `git fetch`. Every later step was skipped, among them `Type check workspace packages` and the CLI transcript check. The closing `Lane verdict` step then exited 1 because `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` was not on disk: the tree was never checked out. `TypeScript Type Check` (job 131564106104) is the aggregator. It printed ok for the other three lanes and failed on `typecheck-workspace` alone. Of the remaining 66 check-runs, ten are skipped (opt-in or path-gated lanes, the dogfood shards among them) and the rest concluded success.
- **What that leaves unanswered on this head.** The per-package `typecheck` task of the affected packages. For `@objectstack/spec` the source half is answered: `Type Check · source gates` concluded success and its step `Type check (@objectstack/spec)` runs `tsc --noEmit`. The test half is not: `check:test-typecheck` is part of the package's `typecheck` script, and its debt file lists three test files this diff edits (`stack.test.ts`, `compose-stacks.test.ts`, `compose-stacks-key-loss.test.ts`). The dependents' `tsc --noEmit` is not answered either. Escalated to the lane seat: the job is re-run to a real verdict before the PR is readied. This record does not read the lane as green.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no separate author note is owed.
- **Branch name.** Answered by the restated claim, comment 6836152532.
- **Both doors judge `packages[]` bodies.** Answered by card Work 2.
- **The top level of a `'preserve'` composition is not judged.** Not answered as the PR states it: ④ S1.
- **`plugin` and the other types are not judged, and a flat composition whose selected manifest is a `plugin` takes every input's apps under that id.** Answered by card Work 4: out of scope here, a decision card if the lane wants it. For that card: the new control test and three moved fixtures (retyped to a `plugin` manifest) now pin this shape as accepted.
- **The object and action conflict arms are untouched.** Verified in the diff: the hunks are the single-app helpers, one class docblock, the option's TSDoc, the `composeStacks` TSDoc and step 3c.
- **File surface.** All 11 files fall inside the claim as restated in comment 6836576990.
- **hotcrm.** The measurement found one caller this change refuses, the flat test view in hotcrm's `test/helpers/composed-stack.ts`. Its route depends on #32827, which is open with no PR. The PR body says the seat ruled this "A" in the card thread; card #32810 carries no such comment. Escalated to the lane seat: put the disposition on the card, and land #32827 no later than the release that carries this change, because the changeset's Fix paragraph names the reader that card adds.
- **Skills-docs follow-up.** `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` is answered by comment 6837415956 (the skills lane takes it when the card lands). `skills/objectstack-platform/references/bootstrap.md` has no card among the inputs; the PR body says the seat files it. Escalated to the seat.
- **`open_questions`.** The PR body raises none.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`**, judged against ADR-0019 D3 as amended, ADR-0130 D4, D6 and the 2026-09-22 addendum, the card's acceptance, and the first consumer of what it emits, the load path.

What holds:

- The card's three acceptance sentences. A flat composition of an app package and a module package with one app each is refused with a finding that names the package, each app with its input, and the `'preserve'` remedy. A `'preserve'` composition of one app per package is not touched: under that option only bodies are judged, and each holds one app. The HotCRM shape (an app package and modules, each with a manifest) takes the same path.
- `selectManifest` agrees with the finding: `'first'` and `'last'` skip an input with no manifest, an index reads that slot only, and a slot with no manifest leaves the result without one, which is not judged, as before.
- The body walk reads the list the result really carries: the concatenated `packages` under a flat option, the preserved entries under `'preserve'`. In strict `defineStack` it reads the parsed `data`, so a body's `apps` is an array there.
- Step 3c runs after the manifest, the `apps` concatenation and the preserved entries exist, and after the artifact pass, the order `defineStack` uses.
- The header, code, status and `issues` agree with the class docblock, the ledger comment and the existing `defineStack` site.

**S1 · should-fix · the top level is judged by the `manifest` option, while the load path decides by whether the result carries `packages[]`.** `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` skips the top level under `'preserve'` and gives this reason: the load path registers the bodies and only the bodies, and the flattened collections beside them, where the emitter keeps any, are a copy of the bodies'. The tree disagrees with both halves.

- `packagesCarryEveryInputCollection`, in the same file, keeps the flattened half exactly where it is not a copy: an input with no manifest, and an input that carries `packages` plus collections of its own. `compose-stacks-manifest-preserve.test.ts` pins both ("keeps the flattened copy when an input has NO manifest to own its collections", "keeps the flattened copy when a `packages`-carrying input declares collections of its own").
- The residual rule (`unclaimedTopLevel` and `MetadataPlugin.registerUnclaimedTopLevel` in `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, called by both boot doors) registers every top-level item that no body declares under the stack's own `manifest.id`, and `apps` is in its field map. Under `'preserve'` that manifest is the last input's, and that package's body already carries its own app.

So `composeStacks([appPackage, extras], { manifest: 'preserve' })`, where `appPackage` defines one app and `extras` is a stack with no manifest that defines one app, is accepted, and at load the app package's id owns two apps. That is the shape the rule removes, and the Console reaches the second app only by name. Composed flat, the same two inputs are refused, and the finding prescribes exactly that `'preserve'` call. The same holds for an input that carries `packages[]` and an app of its own, for example the result of a flat composition this door accepted.

The mirror case over-refuses. Under a flat option, an input that carries `packages[]` together with flattened copies (a `'preserve'` result that kept the additive shape) brings apps its bodies own. The door counts them against the selected manifest and says the composition gives that package N apps, while at load each registers under its body's id and only the unclaimed ones go to the manifest id. The remedy it names still works there, so that half is a wrong sentence, not a wrong prescription.

Owed, one of two. Either judge what registration puts under the artifact's manifest id under every option; the inputs that are assembled into no body are the two cases `packagesCarryEveryInputCollection` already walks. Or correct the docblock, the `composeStacks` TSDoc sentence "the result is held to ADR-0019 D3 as amended" and the reach of the remedy, and card the residual route for the door that reads `unclaimedTopLevel`. Either one moves the head and earns a delta review.

Nits, none of which changes what is accepted or refused:

- **N1 · nit.** The `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` docblock says each input passed its own `defineStack` with one app, and that a single input's own `defineStack` already judged it. Neither is true of an input built with `strict: false`, which `defineStack` does not judge and the single-input return hands back unjudged. The boundary itself is the declared one.
- **N2 · nit.** The `singleAppFinding` docblock says every door judges a package through it, a composed result included. The flat branch restates the predicate inline and writes its own sentence; only the constants are shared.
- **N3 · nit.** The `composeStacks` `@example` still opens with a flat `composeStacks([crm, todo])` as the simple case, and its comment lists what that call throws on without this refusal.
- **N4 · nit.** A finding names a package by `id` alone, so a manifest or body that has a `name` and no `id` (reachable only through `strict: false`) prints as `'undefined'`, while `stackLabel` in the same finding and the load path fall back to `name`.

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`**, judged against the class it describes and the rows around it. The added comment agrees with the code sentence by sentence: two raise sites, one rule, and the `door: 'none'` reading holds, because `composeStacks` has no call site under `packages/*/src` outside `packages/spec`, and the `defineStack` calls there are a shipped template config, a `verify` fixture and the downstream-contract stack, none behind an HTTP handler; `packages/runtime/src` and `packages/rest/src` hold neither. No finding.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.compose-stacks-flat-second-app-refused.ts`**, judged against ADR-0087 D3, the `SemanticMigration` type and the neighbouring entry `18.module-package-second-app-refused.ts`. `surface`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` agree with the code and with ADR-0019's three reasons, and the strings carry no tracker number.

- **N5 · nit.** `replacement` says the artifact's manifest is "still the last input's". That is true of the default. A composition that used `'first'` or an index, both named in `surface`, and follows the entry gets the last input's manifest as the artifact's, a different artifact identity from the one it had (ADR-0130 D6), unless it reorders its inputs. The entry does not say so.

Grades: S1 should-fix; N1 to N5 nit. No must-fix. The nits sit under `packages/spec/src`, so they are left as accepted deviations unless they ride the S1 change.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `91fca555334a5988a46d0f736f95ec24b69a1a80`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.compose-stacks-flat-second-app-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + none

This is a delta round. It follows record 6839703155, rendered on `cf5a8840`, and covers the one commit between that head and this one: five files, the three `hits` files plus `stack.test.ts` and the changeset. It judges whether that commit answers S1 and the nits N1 to N5, and what the commit newly accepts or refuses. Everything else in record 6839703155 stands as written there.

Read for this round: the diff from `cf5a8840` to the head, the 68 check-runs on the head and the steps of the `Type Check · workspace` job, card #32810 (still six comments, none added since the first round) and card #32827. The PR body was written for `cf5a8840` and is not judged against this head. The tests and the changeset were read as evidence and stay the lane seat's ACCEPT. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed: `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `artifactItemSlot`, `claimedArtifactSlots`, `registerUnclaimedTopLevel`), `packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`, and in `stack.zod.ts` the unchanged `isResidualTopLevelItem`, `residualSlotOf`, `preservePackageEntries`, `packagesCarryEveryInputCollection`, `validateSingleApp` and steps 1 to 8 of `composeBuiltStacks`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `composeStacks` now reads the top level of its result by whether the result carries `packages[]`, under every `manifest` option, and no longer by the option. Right: that is the question the load path asks (ADR-0130 D4, `unclaimedTopLevel`).
2. Newly refused relative to `cf5a8840`: a result that carries `packages[]` and keeps a manifest of type `app` or `module`, where the apps of the body with that manifest's id plus the top-level apps that no body declares come to two or more, at least one of them undeclared. Under `'preserve'` that is an input with no manifest that defines an app, or a nested artifact with an app of its own, beside the last input's own app. Under a flat option it is the apps of the inputs composed beside a nested artifact. Right: the residual rule registers each such app under the artifact's manifest id, beside that package's own. Same code `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION`, 422, same `composeStacks` header.
3. Newly accepted relative to `cf5a8840`: a flat composition with a nested artifact among its inputs, whose top-level apps come to two or more only because the nested artifact's flattened copy repeats apps its bodies declare. Right: those apps register under their bodies' ids. `main` accepts this shape too, so the net narrowing against `main` shrinks here.
